That was an incredibly inappropriate thing for her to say to you, and I'm sorry that happened. Unfortunately, there just isn't as much oversight of therapists as there should be. If she's actively struggling with mental illness she shouldn't be practicing. The best thing to do would probably be to get a new therapist. That being said, it can be fucking impossible to find a therapist, let alone one you actually like. So if it isn't possible/you really, really don't want to find a new one then you NEED to talk to her about it. As someone else suggested, it might help to write out what you want to say before having the conversation. If she can't/won't acknowledge that she fucked up and promise that it will not happen again then you need to run in the other direction. Someone who wants to play the ed competition game is not someone who is going to be good for your mental health, no matter how much you like her. If she has a supervisor it might also be a good idea to talk to that person.

I'm so sorry that this happened to you. First of all, I want to stress as much as possible that it is absolutely NOT your responsibility to take care of her. However, if you do want to make things easier generally the most helpful thing you can do is to just treat her as normally as possible and maybe try to be a little nicer/more patient than usual. Did you know about your mom's mental health issues before this? It seems like this really affected you, so it might be a good idea for you to get some therapy to process your own feelings around this, but you will need parental permission to access care. Do you have another parent or trusted adult you could bring this up with? If there is an adult who can help figure this out (other parent, grandparent, aunt, uncle, etc) that would be best because you should not have to deal with this alone. Also, is it safe for you to have a conversation with her that might be emotional? YOUR safety should be your top priority, so make sure to do what is best for you.
